incident: Change Healthcare (UnitedHealth Group / Optum) — ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware, 21 February 2024

sources.title: Testimony of Andrew Witty, CEO UnitedHealth Group, before the U.S. Senate Committee on Finance, 1 May 2024
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (12 Feb, compromised credentials, Citrix remote-access portal, no MFA), lateral movement + exfiltration, ransomware deployed nine days later, data centre connections severed, ransom decision, rebuild (laptops replaced, credentials rotated, data centre network and core services rebuilt), restoration figures (pharmacy 99% by 7 March, payments ~86%, $6.5bn advanced)

sources.title: UnitedHealth Group Form 8-K, Item 1.05, filed 21-22 Feb 2024
sources.what_it_gave: detection moment: 'On February 21, 2024, UnitedHealth Group identified a suspected nation-state associated cyber security threat actor had gained access to some of the Change Healthcare information technology systems' and 'proactively isolated the impacted systems'

sources.title: Cybersecurity Dive, UnitedHealth CEO testimony: tech takeaways (House E&C + Senate Finance hearings, May 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: hops: Citrix remote access server was 'the server through which the cybercriminals were able to get into Change'; credentials likely bought on dark web; prime and backup environments not isolated and both encrypted ('locking up the various backup systems ... really the root cause'); ~40-year-old claims/payment systems; cloud elements recovered quickly; data on about one third of Americans

sources.title: TechTarget, Change Healthcare breached via Citrix portal with no MFA (May 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: 12 Feb access, 21 Feb ransomware/disclosure, data centres shut down, encryption contained to Change network, $872m Q1 2024 cost (UHG earnings), 30,000+ pharmacies served

sources.title: TechCrunch, How the ransomware attack at Change Healthcare went down: a timeline (updated 27 Jan 2025)
sources.what_it_gave: 29 Feb UHG attribution to ALPHV/BlackCat; affiliate claim of $22m Bitcoin payment 3 March; RansomHub second extortion April; 100m (Oct 2024) then 190m (Jan 2025) individuals affected; Nebraska complaint: low-level customer support account without MFA, attackers could 'travel freely between servers'

sources.title: CISA/FBI/HHS joint advisory AA23-353A, #StopRansomware: ALPHV Blackcat (Dec 2023, updated Feb 2024)
sources.what_it_gave: ALPHV TTP reference for technique IDs (valid accounts T1078, external remote services T1133, remote services T1021, exfiltration T1567, encryption T1486); NOTE: fetch was blocked in this session, mapping relies on the advisory's published content

narrative_before: On 12 February 2024 'criminals used compromised credentials to remotely access a Change Healthcare Citrix portal, an application used to enable remote access to desktops. The portal did not have multi-factor authentication' (Witty, Senate Finance testimony). Over the next nine days the attackers 'moved laterally within the systems in more sophisticated ways and exfiltrated data'; because Change's prime and backup environments were not isolated, the backups were encrypted too, which Witty called 'really the root cause' of the long recovery (Cybersecurity Dive). On 21 February 2024 ALPHV/BlackCat deployed ransomware 'encrypting Change's systems so we could not access them'; the same day UnitedHealth 'identified a suspected nation-state associated cyber security threat actor' and 'proactively isolated the impacted systems', severing Change's data-centre connections so that malware did not spread beyond Change (8-K; testimony). Pharmacy claims, medical claims and payment processing for much of the US stopped: 99% of pre-incident pharmacies were only back by 7 March, payments were at ~86% of pre-incident levels at the time of the hearing, and UHG had advanced more than $6.5bn to providers (testimony). UHG confirmed on 29 February the actor was ALPHV/BlackCat, paid a ransom (an affiliate cited a $22m Bitcoin transaction), booked $872m of Q1 2024 costs, and ultimately notified ~190 million people (TechCrunch; TechTarget).

detection_moments.description: 21 February 2024: first and only defender detection — ransomware is deployed inside Change's IT environment and UHG identifies the intrusion the same day, isolating Change's data centres from the rest of UHG. Nine days of undetected access (12-21 Feb) preceded it; no earlier alert is described in any public source. Citrix portal = initial access via valid credentials (5); desktop = lateral foothold (6); encrypted servers incl. backups = T1486 (9).
detection_moments.evidence: 'On February 21, 2024, UnitedHealth Group identified a suspected nation-state associated cyber security threat actor had gained access to some of the Change Healthcare information technology systems ... proactively isolated the impacted systems' (UHG Form 8-K Item 1.05); 'Ransomware was deployed nine days later' and 'encrypting Change's systems so we could not access them' (Witty Senate testimony); 'the attack locking up the various backup systems ... really the root cause' (Witty, per Cybersecurity Dive).

attack_path: Compromised credentials (likely bought on the dark web) used against the Citrix remote-access portal with no MFA, 12 Feb 2024 — T1078, T1133
Citrix portal 'used to enable remote access to desktops'; attacker lands on an internal desktop session under a low-level customer-support account — T1021.001
'moved laterally within the systems in more sophisticated ways' across Change's data-centre network over nine days — T1021
Prime and backup environments not isolated; backup systems reached and later encrypted — T1021, T1490
Data exfiltration (data on ~1/3 of Americans) then ALPHV ransomware deployed 21 Feb across claims, payment and core services — T1567, T1486
ambiguities: Public sources never name individual internal hosts; srv_core_1..3, pc_desktop_1..3 and pc_laptop_1..3 are generic placeholders for 'Change Healthcare's data center network and core services', the Citrix-published desktops and the 'thousands of laptops' replaced (rule 1, 3-10 per generic group).

No Active Directory / domain controller is named in testimony or filings; 'rotated credentials' implies domain credentials were at risk but no source says domain credentials were used for lateral movement, so no 'dc' machine and no workstation -> dc links were added.

The order of lateral hops between the desktop, core servers, claims platforms and backups is not public; the links fan out from a single srv_core_1 pivot as the simplest structure consistent with 'moved laterally ... in more sophisticated ways' and 'travel freely between servers' (Nebraska complaint via TechCrunch).

srv_backup is modelled as a single shared replica for all three core services; which services the backups covered is not stated. Replicas = 2 only because Witty explicitly said backup systems existed (and were encrypted).
Exfiltration method/staging host is not public (ALPHV commonly uses rclone/Mega per AA23-353A); no exfil host added.
The $22m ransom figure is an ALPHV affiliate's claim about a Bitcoin transaction (TechCrunch); UHG confirmed paying but never stated the amount.
190 million affected (Jan 2025) comes from UHG's updated HHS breach notice, not from the May 2024 testimony, which said 'about one third' of Americans.

Only one detection moment exists: the 8-K and testimony place discovery on 21 Feb, coincident with ransomware deployment; hence encrypted hosts carry T1486 risk 9 at that moment. Hosts are limited to Change's own environment ('contained the blast radius to just Change').
CISA AA23-353A could not be fetched in this session; it is cited only as the ALPHV technique reference.

Eligibility and other Change products were disrupted according to press reports but are not itemised in the testimony retrieved, so only pharmacy claims, medical claims and payments are modelled as services.
